resolutions.researcher_notes: EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects database (sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)') carries the row 'North Texas Pipeline Expansion/Old Ocean Pipeline' (operators Enterprise, Energy Transfer Partners; State TX; Authority TX RRC), with 'Completed Date' = 2019-01-15 and 'Year In Service Date' = 2019 -- matching the sheet's StartYear1 exactly. The row's own Project Notes read: 'Service will be resumed on Old Ocean Pipeline (160 MMcf/d) from Dallas to Gulf Coast (done 2Q 2018); expansion on North Texas pipeline to provide Permian takeaway capacity, filling Old Ocean (expected 4Q2018)' -- i.e. EIA's own database explains the two-stage timeline: the pipeline itself physically resumed flowing gas in 2Q 2018 (this is what the seed OGJ article, verified live, and the seed NaturalGasIntel 2022 article both describe as 'reactivation'/'2018'), while the associated North Texas expansion that fills it to capacity is the piece EIA formally logs as completed/in-service Jan 2019 -- reconciling why GEM's own StartYear1 (2019) differs from the initial-flow date reported in 2018 trade press. Single source (one EIA record), so medium tier, independent: false; this is a government project-tracking database, not the applicant's own filing, so treated as an independent origin from the OGJ/NGI trade-press pair even though not stacked with them here. CONCERN (informational only, no value changed): OGJ (May 2018, https://www.ogj.com/articles/2018/05/epp-etp-combine-to-revive-old-ocean-pipeline-to-move-permian-supply.html, verified live) and NaturalGasIntel (Jul 2022, describing the same pipeline via its 240-mile length and Maypearl-to-Sweeny endpoints, which match the sheet's LengthKnown and Start/EndLocation exactly) both frame the pipeline as reactivated in 2018, not 2019 -- worth a human note that '2019' likely reflects the expansion/fill-to-capacity milestone rather than first gas flow, per the EIA notes text above.
